[heading][color=#ffff00]Description[/color][/heading]
This mod adds full voice acting to the game using the Windows Text-to-Speech (SAPI5) voices installed on your system.
The more voices you have installed, the greater the variety of speech styles, accents, and characters the mod can simulate. If you only have two voices installed, don't expect much diversity.
You can install additional free Windows voices from your Windows language settings, or download and install them directly through my MCM mod. After installing new voices, remember to synchronize them in the MCM.
The mod also supports multiple languages. Text written in those languages will be spoken correctly, as long as you have the corresponding Windows TTS voice installed. The game automatically uses the appropriate system voice for each supported language whenever possible.
[b]In short:[/b]

[left]Tutorial: Install TTS Voices in Windows for SMAPI
Mods
SimpleVioiceTTS — Stardew Valley
1. The Problem: OneCore vs SAPI5
Windows has TWO separate Text-to-Speech engines:
• SAPI5 (old, 2000): Used by SpVoice COM. Only sees Desktop voices in English (David, Zira).
• OneCore (modern, Win10/11): Voices in Spanish, Japanese, German, etc.
SpVoice (the one you use in C# with Type.GetTypeFromProgID("Sapi.SpVoice")) is BLIND
to OneCore voices. This tutorial installs the OneCore voices and exposes them to SAPI5 via
registry.
2. Step 1 — Activate Windows Services
BITS and wuauserv must be running to download language packages. Run PowerShell as
[color=#ff0000]Administrator:[/color]
[color=#00ffff]Start-Service BITS
Get-Service BITS[/color]
[color=#00ffff]Get-Service wuauserv[/color]
Start-Service wuauserv # if stopped
Important: If wuauserv does not start, ignore it; BITS is the critical service for the
download.
3. Step 2 — List Available Voices
See which voice packages Microsoft has for your system:
Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like "*Speech*"

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50236/50236-1785972448-610362964.png[/img]
Look for lines like Language.TextToSpeech~~~es-ES~0.0.1.0 (Spanish) or ~ja-JP~
(Japanese).
4. Step 3 — Install Voices by Language
Install ALL voices for a language (example Spanish):
Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object {$_.State -eq "NotPresent" -and $_.Name -like "Langu
To install ALL voices for ALL languages:
Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object {$_.State -eq "NotPresent" -and $_.Name -like "Langu
Attention: The download may take 5–15 minutes depending on your connection.
5. Blocks by Language (Copy & Paste)

block of the language you need and paste it into PowerShell as Administrator.

Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name Language.TextToSpeech~~~de-DE~0.0.1.0[/color]

6. Step 4 — Verify OneCore Installation
Check that the voices appear as Installed:
Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like "*Speech*"
7. Step 5 — Expose OneCore to SAPI5 (The Trick)
SpVoice only reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Speech\Voices\Tokens. OneCore voices are
in Speech_OneCore. We copy the registry keys with this script:
[color=#00ffff]# Export OneCore voices
reg export "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Speech_OneCore\Voices\Tokens" "$env:TEMP\onecore_voices.reg"
# Replace paths and save for SAPI5
$content = Get-Content "$env:TEMP\onecore_voices.reg" -Raw
$content = $content -replace 'Speech_OneCore', 'Speech'
$content = $content -replace 'Speech\Isolated', 'Speech'
Set-Content "$env:TEMP\sapi5_voices.reg" $content -Force
# Import to SAPI5
reg import "$env:TEMP\sapi5_voices.reg"
Write-Host "Voices copied. Restart SMAPI.[/color]
Manual alternative: Open regedit, export Speech_OneCore\Voices\Tokens, replace
"Speech_OneCore" with "Speech" in the .reg file, and import it.
8. Step 6 — Verify in Your SMAPI Mod
Add this method to your SapiTTS.cs class to list voices in the console:
[color=#00ffff]public void ListVoices()
{
var voices = _voice.GetVoices();
for (int i = 0; i < voices.Count; i++)
{
dynamic v = voices.Item(i);
Console.WriteLine($"[TTS][{i}] {v.GetDescription()}");
}
}[/color]
Call it in ModEntry.Entry(): _tts.ListVoices(); and check the SMAPI console.
